1.10 rebuilt middleware as an onion, "to solve the lack of strict request/response layering" (`docs/releases/1.10.txt`).

A response that one middleware's `process_request` returned still passed through the `process_response` of every middleware, those that never saw the request among them (`deps:final/0005-improved-middleware.rst`).

`BaseHandler.load_middleware` builds the nest once (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.load_middleware`; [Building the middleware chain](../handlers/chain.md)).
At this commit it is the base of all Django's middleware but `RemoteUserMiddleware` and its subclass `PersistentRemoteUserMiddleware` (`django/middleware/__init__.py:MiddlewareMixin`).
It lived in `django.utils.deprecation`, the module of the deprecation warnings, until 6.2 moved it to `django.middleware` (`django/utils/deprecation.py:__getattr__`).

Instead exceptions are converted to responses "before and after every middleware", so that a layer may raise `Http404` and count on a response from the layer inside (`deps:final/0005-improved-middleware.rst`).
The conversion is `convert_exception_to_response`, wrapped around each layer as the chain is built (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:convert_exception_to_response`).

Each part was to pass through stages: first its synchronous code behind an asynchronous wrapper that runs it in a thread, later asynchronous code behind a synchronous wrapper (`deps:accepted/0009-async.rst`).
Code marked as unsafe, such as the ORM's, refused to run where an event loop was running (`docs/releases/3.0.txt`).

At this commit they still do: `QuerySet.aget` runs `QuerySet.get` through `sync_to_async`, "sync-native, with an async wrapper" in DEP 9's words (`django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet.aget`; [The asynchronous methods of a queryset](../querysets/async.md)).
Python cannot give one name both a synchronous and an asynchronous body, so DEP 9 proposed a suffix, get_async beside get, as the easiest to check in review (`deps:accepted/0009-async.rst`).
